Billing Department, Lakeside General Hospital (fictional)

Re: Request for billing review and adjustment
Patient: Sample Patient A (fictional)
Payer: Self-pay
Total billed: $4,080

To the Billing Department:

I have reviewed my itemized bill and found four lines that appear to be billed in error. I respectfully ask that you review them and adjust my account as described below.

Line 1 (CPT 99285, Emergency visit, high complexity): Line 1 charges $2,400 per unit for "Emergency visit, high complexity", but the hospital's own posted cash price is $1,650. The overcharge is $750.
Basis: Hospital's posted standard charges (cash price) under the federal hospital price transparency rule, 45 CFR Part 180: $1,650 per unit.

Line 5 (CPT 80048, Basic metabolic blood panel (8 tests)): Line 5 ("Basic metabolic blood panel (8 tests)") is billed separately, but line 4 ("Comprehensive metabolic blood panel (14 tests)") already includes it. Every test in the basic panel is already part of the comprehensive panel. The overcharge is $85.
Basis: Bundling rule modeled on CMS NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits: 80053 includes 80048.

Line 7 (CPT 85025, Complete blood count with differential): "Complete blood count with differential" appears again on line 7, same day as line 6, with no modifier saying it was repeated on purpose. The overcharge is $60.
Basis: Duplicate charge: same code, same date of service, no repeat-test modifier (91, 76 or 77).

Line 8 (CPT 84484, Troponin (heart muscle damage) blood test): Line 8 bills 5 units of "Troponin (heart muscle damage) blood test" in one day; the limit is 3. That is 2 extra units at $95 each. The overcharge is $190.
Basis: Max-units rule modeled on CMS Medically Unlikely Edits: 84484 allows 3 per day.

In total, I am requesting an adjustment of $1,085 to my bill (Line 1: $750; Line 5: $85; Line 7: $60; Line 8: $190).

Please send me a corrected itemized bill, or a written explanation if you believe any of these charges are correct. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
Sample Patient A (fictional)

To the Billing Department:

I have reviewed my itemized bill and am writing to ask that you review the four lines below, which appear to be billed incorrectly. I appreciate your attention to this.

Line 1 (CPT 73562, Knee X-ray, three views): This line charges $395 per unit, but the hospital's own posted cash price is $280. The difference is $115.
Basis: Hospital's posted standard charges (cash price) under the federal hospital price transparency rule, 45 CFR Part 180: $280 per unit.

Line 3 (CPT 29881, Knee arthroscopy, trimming one meniscus): This line is billed separately, but Line 2 (Knee arthroscopy, trimming both menisci) already includes it. Trimming both menisci already includes trimming one meniscus. The amount in question is $9,800.
Basis: Bundling rule modeled on CMS NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits: 29880 includes 29881.

Line 4 (CPT 20610, Large joint injection or fluid removal): This line is billed separately, but Line 2 (Knee arthroscopy, trimming both menisci) already includes it. A joint injection in the same knee during arthroscopy is part of the surgery. The amount in question is $420.
Basis: Bundling rule modeled on CMS NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits: 29880 includes 20610.

Line 5 (HCPCS J1885, Pain-relief injection (ketorolac), per 15 mg): This line bills 12 units in one day, but the limit is 8. The 4 extra units at $25 each come to $100.
Basis: Max-units rule modeled on CMS Medically Unlikely Edits: J1885 allows 8 per day.

Please review these lines, remove or correct the charges noted above, and send me a corrected itemized bill showing the adjusted total. If you disagree with any of these findings, please explain in writing which line you disagree with and why.
